mostWorthwhile.text: Adding oxygen to the red cells was most worthwhile: the planned inset and prose show haemoglobin binding and releasing oxygen, then connect release to working tissues.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making plasma was predictable, and its picture added little explanation beyond showing particles and proteins in fluid.

surprise.text: The developing-cell cutaway linked haemoglobin assembly to maturation into nucleus-free red cells; I had been unsure whether maturation would happen in that step.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt entirely purposeless, but adding white cells and platelets was less clearly connected to the oxygen-carrying goal. Their roles were not explained.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how circulation brings oxygen carriers close to cells, though the sample-assembly steps themselves were fairly predictable.
